engineeringDecision: Retain the two accepted PR #47 optimizations. No follow-up candidate was added.

interpretation.scope: Four separate synthetic Future collections with independently frozen builds, on an eight-processor JVM. All host load readings are 1/5/15-minute averages. All collections are diagnostic and remain unpooled. The PR47 comparison with v11 measures their aggregate implementation difference.
interpretation.selection: Settled missed its inline improvement rule. Direct passed the allocation screen, submitted supplement and guarded-mixed budgets. Completion missed the original contention p99 budget and has an incompatible helper class target.
interpretation.engineeringDecision: Keep the PR47 runtime as the default and retain direct as a local option for allocation-sensitive use. Direct consistently saved bytes but reduced median throughput and raised delivery p99 on the guarded-mixed workload. The formal screen qualifies direct for review; it does not require adoption.

protocol.statistics: Report arm median and min/max. Direction counts compare arms within the same round. Each row retains its collection and original label. All three budgets use ratios against the workload-specific reference.

criteria.settled: Both inline and submitted workloads must pass budgets. Inline requires ≥2% throughput improvement or ≥5% delivery-p99 improvement, with at least four of six pairs improving on the qualifying metric.
criteria.allocation: All four workloads must pass against PR47. Four-writer savings ≥12 B for direct, ≥36 B for completion; completion also requires ≥84 B in eight-extension workload. Both target workloads require lower bytes in at least 2/3 pairs. If both qualify, prefer completion at ≥2× direct’s contention savings; otherwise prefer direct.
criteria.submitted: Only the selected allocation arm runs. All budgets plus at least four of six lower-allocation pairs and ≥12 B savings for direct (≥36 B for completion).
criteria.guarded: Only direct can advance. Test direct against all three PR47 guardrails. Classify the standalone v11 comparison descriptively and preserve a failure if it occurs.

protocol.fixtureDifferences: Canonical callbacks run inline. The submitted fixture schedules callback bodies on the same worker pool, without assuming every Future takes the asynchronous handoff. Guarded mixed alternates state and message from four writers and verifies synchronous successful guards, per-writer sequence, handler order, final state identity and teardown. No slow authorization I/O, browser transport or application latency is measured.

+   * Runs one delayed Unit step and observes its terminal result. Only the

futureObservation.publicApiAndApplicability: unit2 adds a package-internal companion helper. Only the private default Future effect and the exact Future.unit singleton can skip flattening. An explicit thunk constructs the step once. Instrumented/delegating/custom effects retain runAsync(delayAsync(...)); non-singleton returned Futures retain flattening, and thrown construction preserves the original normalization. Every completion still uses runAsync/onComplete. Match only replaces Either.left.foreach with explicit Left/Right dispatch.

measurement.method: Ratios of arm medians versus PR47 within the same workload and collection. Per-JVM values, pre/post loads and paired order remain available. No pooling or replacement of rows.
measurement.protocolText:
# Profile-guided serial lane comparisons

All collections are diagnostic. The reference is PR #47 at `b6f11ca04224eb6954e62b31b31a69da97e75ab1` (`received`). Each independent arm has exactly its stated patch on that parent: `unit2-on-pr47.patch` uses an explicitly typed thunk at the GADT boundary, while `left-match-on-pr47.patch` changes the error-result dispatch. The earlier `unit` prototype failed its functional tests and is excluded. Every admitted arm passes the core/CE3/ZIO2 extension and lane suites plus the purity check. The effect change must additionally pass the full effect suite, including its new observation cases. Verify frozen classpaths, expected source diffs, and common fixture overlays before and after every collection. Keep partial and failed runs.

**Independent screening.** Use 36 fresh JVMs. Inline uses the unmodified canonical benchmark in six balanced permutations. Submitted uses the prebuilt shared async benchmark, and fallback uses the prebuilt guarded-precompleted benchmark, each in three rotating orders. For rounds 1–6 run the inline permutation; in rounds 1, 3 and 5 also run one submitted and one fallback permutation (submitted first, fallback first, submitted first, respectively). The six inline orders are PUM, UMP, MPU, MUP, UPM, PMU (P = PR47, U = unit2, M = match); the two other workloads each use PUM, UMP, MPU. All use one view, four writers, three extensions, a 1024-notification window, zero artificial callback work, five seconds of warmup and five of measurement in a 256 MiB fixed G1 heap with eight reported processors. Preserve admission/delivery order and count checks, histogram and producer-allocation checks, and the guarded fixtures' initial, per-kind and teardown checks. Save every raw row, JFR digest, before/after UTC/load sample, and full input evidence.

**Screen decision.** For each metric use the ratio of independent per-arm medians within each workload. Both candidates require ≥95% throughput, ≤110% delivery p99 and ≤110% allocation on all three modes against PR47. Unit2 additionally requires ≥97% throughput and ≤107% p99 on submitted and fallback. Its inline benefit must be ≥5% throughput, ≥10% lower delivery p99, or ≥96 B/notification saved with median throughput and p99 at least as good as PR47. Match instead requires ≥2% throughput, ≥5% lower p99, or ≥16 B/notification saved with throughput ≥99% and p99 ≤105%. The metric that earns each benefit must improve in at least four of six matched inline rounds.

When both qualify, select match unless unit2 has median throughput and delivery p99 at least as good as match and offers ≥5 additional percentage points of throughput or p99 improvement (using the common PR47 denominator) or ≥64 more B/notification saved on inline. A valid miss stands. If neither qualifies, stop.

**Confirmation.** Only the unchanged winner can proceed. Run the release harness on its four canonical workloads, three alternating fresh pairs each (24 JVMs), with identical JVM flags and timing. Require the ordinary 95%/110%/110% budgets across all four workloads and another movement in the favorable direction for at least one benefit that earned selection, on the contended workload. A passing unit2 must also pass six fresh alternating pairs of the successful guarded-mixed workload with the ordinary budgets against PR47. Match has no additional mixed confirmation. No combining results across modes, replacing failed results, fallback candidate promotion, or release-qualification claim.

The command reported 0.40 seconds elapsed; the disassembly file was completed at 06:22:37.820 UTC. Preserve its row and the predeclared screen. An unchanged screen miss cannot be converted into a selection by repeating it.

If and only if unit2 qualifies, add an independent diagnostic pair series on the guarded-precompleted fallback against the exact same PR47 parent: six fresh alternating pairs, the same disabled-singleton workload, fixture and JVM flags, requiring throughput >=97%, p99 <=107% and allocation <=110%. Report both outcomes separately. If either fallback series misses, do not recommend unit2 on that evidence. The other arm's independent trials are unaffected by this incidental process. nativeBackends.protocol:
# CE3 and ZIO2 delivery fallback qualification

Compare frozen PR 47 (received) with frozen unit2 within each backend. Each backend/arm pair uses the same listener fixture, the same native adapter and the same dependency overlay. This is a diagnostic check of the interpreter fallback. Performance comparisons apply only between the two arms on one backend.

The view is unguarded, with four writer threads, three handlers, 1,024 permits, four lane workers and the default CE3 or ZIO2 native runtime. Every callback's ordering check, counter and final delivery timestamp are evaluated inside the adapter's lazy effect (`IO3Effect.delay` or `Zio2Effect.delay`). There is no synthetic callback CPU work. Native fibers and their scheduler perform normal execution. The 5-second warmup and 5-second measurement each use a new view inside the same JVM. Delivery ends inside the third handler; throughput counts admitted notifications through the full drain. The fixture checks per-writer sequence, registration order, exact callback counts, ready state, bounded backlog drain, reverse teardown with each handler's last state, the empty lane and absence of reported warnings or errors.

Run three fresh-JVM pairs per backend; parent first in rounds 1 and 3, candidate first in round 2. All 12 rows must pass correctness. For **each** backend, the ratio of candidate to parent median must be at least 95% for throughput and at most 110% for p99 delivery. Both backends must meet both limits before advancing this candidate. Report the unrounded ratios, separate arm medians, ranges and all raw rows. Keep failed rows. Smoke runs are separate and do not count. Do not pool CE3 with ZIO2 or with the Future workloads. No allocation or release-gate claim is made; the native runtimes own worker pools and lifetimes.
nativeBackends.scope: Backend timings compare each actual adapter with the identical adapter on PR #47; a passing backend cannot reverse the guarded-precompleted Future throughput miss.
